name: a diamond has no cycle and orders cited notes first
why: a links to b and c, both link to d. A visited-set check would see d twice and report a cycle; three-colour search finds d black (finished), not grey, the second time.

queries.why: No edge reaches a grey node.
An acyclic graph has only singleton components, numbered by smallest member, which for singletons is ID order.
Only d links to nothing, so it is placed first. That makes b and c ready; b is the smaller ID. Then a. Layers: d links to nothing (0), b and c link to d (1), a links to layer 1 (2).
a's prerequisites are everything it reaches: b, c, d. They come in topological order with a last. d is reached in two hops through b or c; via is the smaller, b.
One component, and it holds the root a.
Two paths of two hops. Walking back from d, the smallest-ID neighbour one hop closer to a is b.
Undirected this is the 4-cycle a-b-d-c. Opposite corners (a,d) and (b,c) are 2 apart; (a,d) is the lexicographically smaller pair.
For a: of the pairs among b, c, d only (b,c) is not adjacent, and one of its two shortest paths passes through a, so a scores 1/2 over 3 pairs = 1/6. The 4-cycle is symmetric.
